purpose.text: Turns objectives into approved money: how much goes to which portfolio, value stream, shared platform or cross-portfolio investment, and within which [[guardrail|guardrails]]. It keeps [[target]], [[budget]], [[forecast]] and [[actual-cost|actuals]] apart, so that funding decisions can be traced to what was spent and achieved.

items.responsibility: Sets the overall technology budget and the IT cost target; owns budgeting rules and capitalisation.
Allocates budgets to portfolios, sets guardrails, approves cross-portfolio investments and their funding split.
Represents the technology view, including mandatory investments for security, resilience and lifecycle.
Funds value streams within the portfolio budget and adjusts within guardrails.
Provides run cost, unit cost and cost forecasts as input; does not decide on funding.
Receive a stable budget and report capacity needs and constraints.

items.what: Objectives and investment themes set funding priorities.
Run cost, unit cost and cost forecast inform realistic budgets.
End-of-life technologies and risks require mandatory investment.
Results and variances trigger continued funding, reallocation or stop.
IT cost target and the approved budget frame.
Portfolio budgets, guardrails and funding splits define what can be prioritised.
Value stream budgets give stable delivery capacity.

items.text: Investment themes exist, but budgets are rolled forward from last year instead of following the themes.
Budgets are planned by portfolio, actuals are reported by cost centre – nobody can say whether a portfolio is on budget.
Budgets are approved per project while delivery runs in long-lived teams – money and capacity do not match.
A cross-portfolio investment is funded by the lead portfolio only; contributing portfolios do not plan capacity for their share.
Mandatory lifecycle and security investments compete with growth initiatives without their own guardrail and keep being postponed.
Forecast deviations are discussed in finance reviews but do not lead to reallocation decisions.

statements.text: Lean budgets fund value streams instead of projects, and each portfolio operates within an approved budget.
Larger enterprises may manage multiple portfolios.
Lean budgets can contain both CapEx and OpEx; finance should be involved early.
Strategic portfolio management is listed by the TBM Council as a standard connected to TBM.
An enterprise level above several portfolios that sets portfolio budgets, guardrails and funding splits is our synthesis, not a framework requirement.
SAFe's specific guardrails have not been verified against the source; the guardrails here are described generically.

fitsWhen: Several portfolios share platforms or run cross-portfolio investments.
Delivery is organised in long-lived value streams or teams.
adaptWhen: Only one portfolio exists (compact variant): enterprise and portfolio funding merge into one decision.
Delivery is project-based: funding per project remains; value stream funding is a target picture, not a given.
